policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Μαριάμ and Μαρία are alternate forms of the same name; ASV 'Mary' renders either.
Word order of ὧραί εἰσιν only; ASV 'Are there not twelve hours in the day?' does not track Greek order.
ASV 'The disciples therefore said unto him' has the dative object 'unto him' (αὐτῷ) and no possessive 'his disciples' (αὐτοῦ).
Word order of ἤδη ἡμέρας only; ASV 'four days already' does not distinguish the Greek sequence.
Presence of the article with Βηθανία is not rendered in English; ASV 'Now Bethany was' is silent on it.
ASV's connective 'and' renders either the postpositive δέ or the prepositive καί.
ASV 'had come to Martha and Mary' is the standard rendering of both the plain accusative and the τὰς περί idiom; no wording distinguishes them.
Μαριάμ and Μαρίαν are alternate forms of the same name; ASV 'Mary' renders either.
ASV 'their brother' is the idiomatic English for the articular τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ as well as for the explicit αὐτῶν; the possessive does not distinguish the readings.
Μαρία and Μαριάμ are alternate forms of the same name; ASV 'Mary' renders either.
Article with the personal name Μάρθα is not rendered; ASV 'Martha therefore said' is silent on it.
Article with Ἰησοῦν is not rendered; ASV 'unto Jesus' is silent on it.
ASV 'my brother had not died' is the ordinary English of a past contrary-to-fact clause and fits both the aorist ἀπέθανεν and the pluperfect ἐτεθνήκει; word order is not rendered.
ASV 'And even now I know' supplies a light narrative connective; it neither requires nor excludes an adversative ἀλλά.
Article with Μάρθα is not rendered; ASV 'Martha saith unto him' is silent on it.
ASV 'when she had said this' is singular, rendering τοῦτο and not the plural ταῦτα ('these things').
Μαριάμ and Μαρίαν are alternate forms of the same name; ASV 'Mary' renders either. The mapped note is an alternative_rendering about English word order and decides nothing.
ASV's opening 'And' is a narrative connective it supplies freely; it does not require δέ.
ASV 'arose quickly' is past, rendering the aorist ἠγέρθη; ASV renders Johannine historic presents as presents ('Jesus saith', 'Martha saith'), so ἐγείρεται would have appeared as 'ariseth'.
ASV 'and went unto him' is past, rendering the imperfect ἤρχετο; the present ἔρχεται would have been rendered 'cometh' on ASV's practice with historic presents in this chapter.
ASV 'but was still in the place' renders ἔτι, which the alternative omits.
Μαριάμ and Μαρίαν are alternate forms of the same name; ASV 'Mary' renders either.
ASV 'supposing that she was going unto the tomb' renders δόξαντες; λέγοντες would give 'saying'.
Μαριάμ and Μαρία are alternate forms of the same name; ASV 'Mary' renders either.
Article with Ἰησοῦς is not rendered; ASV 'where Jesus was' is silent on it.
ASV 'fell down at his feet' renders πρός and εἰς alike in this idiom.
Word order only; ASV 'my brother had not died' does not track the Greek sequence.
τετελευτηκότος, τελευτηκότος, and τεθνηκότος all mean 'him that was dead', which is ASV's wording; the mapped note is a greek_gloss on 'the body decayeth'.
ὄψῃ and ὄψει are alternate second-person forms of the same verb; ASV 'thou shouldest see' renders either.
ASV 'So they took away the stone' lacks any equivalent of the added οὗ ἦν ὁ τεθνηκὼς κειμένος ('where the dead was laid').
ASV begins the verse 'He that was dead came forth' with no connective, rendering ἐξῆλθεν without the initial Καί.
Word order only; ASV 'Jesus saith unto them' does not track the Greek sequence.
ASV 'Loose him, and let him go' gives an unitalicized object pronoun with both verbs; the alternative leaves the second verb without αὐτόν, which ASV would have supplied in italics.
Μαριάμ and Μαρίαν are alternate forms of the same name; ASV 'Mary' renders either.
ASV text reads the singular 'that which he did' (ὅ), and the mapped textual_variant note puts the plural 'the things which he did' (ἅ) in the margin as the reading of many ancient authorities.
ASV 'beheld that which he did' has the pronoun subject only; it does not render the added ὁ Ἰησοῦς, unlike v. 46 where 'Jesus' is named.
Article with Ἰησοῦς is not rendered; ASV 'the things which Jesus had done' is silent on it.
Word order only; ASV 'this man doeth many signs' does not track the Greek sequence.
ASV 'nor do ye take account' renders λογίζεσθε and the compound διαλογίζεσθε alike.
ASV 'it is expedient for you' renders the second-person ὑμῖν, not the first-person ἡμῖν ('for us').
ASV 'they took counsel' renders ἐβουλεύσαντο and the compound συνεβουλεύσαντο alike.
Article and word order only; ASV 'Jesus therefore' renders either arrangement.
ASV 'there he tarried' renders ἔμεινεν and διέτριβεν alike.
ASV 'with the disciples' has the article and no possessive, so it does not render the added αὐτοῦ ('his disciples').
ASV 'Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given commandment' carries no adverbial 'also', which the added καί would supply.
'Had given commandment' is a number-neutral English idiom in ASV usage and renders the plural ἐντολάς as well as the singular ἐντολήν.
